title: Pricing by hours per project for Solar panel cleaning
audience: Owners and crew leads who quote solar panel cleaning and need a price that covers cost, roof access, warranty checks and a margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour for solar panel cleaning from your own figures
Estimate job hours by panel count, storey and access, including set-up, photographs and the warranty note
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis, access lines and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit for solar work
instruction.body: A panel clean is mostly time on the roof and the set-up that makes the roof access safe, plus the photographs and the warranty note. Panel count matters, but access and storey often change the time more. Start from hours. No current per-panel price from a government or trade body was found, and the only per-panel figure in this research is a 2016-origin article, so do not use a per-panel figure to set the price.

instruction.heading: Build your cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the total cost of running the round by the chargeable hours in the same period. Include wages with on-costs, the vehicle, water supply and storage, the soft brush and water-only equipment, access equipment and its inspection, insurance, phone, software and administration. Use chargeable hours only. Employee pay rates and on-costs may be set by an award or enterprise agreement; that point is unconfirmed here, so check it for each worker before using any figure.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours by array and access
instruction.body: Split each job into the array (count the panels and note any tilted or flat sections), the access set-up for each storey, the cleaning itself, before-and-after photographs, the written note, travel and a checking allowance. Estimate each in a range. Add a set allowance for delays, such as a blocked access route, a roof that is not safe to walk, or a second array the client did not mention. Xero's guide suggests 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work (stated by the source; the BP-05 research flags whether that range is acceptable). Record actual hours by task.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price
instruction.body: Multiply the total hours by the cost per productive hour to get the job cost. Divide by one minus your target margin to get the price. Apply the materials policy and the minimum charge. Show the access and the warranty note as named lines. Do not price any electrical check under the cleaning line.

instruction.heading: Do not convert a price into a per-panel rate
instruction.body: A job price divided by the panel count gives a per-panel figure for that job only. It is not a market rate, and it changes with array layout, storey and access. Do not carry it to other sites without your own records for those sites.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest
instruction.body: A solar quote states the panel count, the storey and access, the hours or price basis, the water-only method, the warranty check, the exclusions (electrical work and any chemical not approved for panels), what the client must provide, and how long the quote is valid. Quotes issued without a site visit are estimates, so say so.

procedure: Gather the year's total round costs and the chargeable hours achieved in the same period.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours to get the cost per productive hour.
Count the panels and record the storey and access at the site visit, then estimate the time for each task as a range.
Add access set-up, photographs, the written note, travel and checking time as named lines.
Multiply total hours by the cost per productive hour, then divide by one minus the margin.
Apply the materials policy and the minimum charge.
Write the quote with array details, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
Record actual hours after each job and compare them with the estimate.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only, not market rates. A 20-panel single-storey roof, with access checked at the site visit. The owner estimates 1.5 hours on the roof for cleaning and photographs, 0.5 hours of access set-up and 0.5 hours of travel, a total of 2.5 hours. The owner's cost per productive hour is $60 AUD (illustrative). The target margin on price is 25 per cent (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the job cost, what is the price with a 25 per cent margin on price, and why must the result not be turned into a per-panel rate for other sites?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cost is 2.5 hours multiplied by $60 AUD, which is $150 AUD. The price is $150 divided by 0.75, which is $200 AUD. That is an illustrative price for this array and access only. Dividing it by 20 panels gives a per-panel figure, but that figure belongs to this job, with this access and these hours. It must not be used for another site without that site's own hours. The access line is confirmed against the Victorian working-at-height rule before the quote is issued.

equipmentAndPpe: Quote worksheet or spreadsheet with lines for array, access, photographs and the warranty note
Time log for each job, with estimated and actual columns
Water-only cleaning equipment, with no pressure hose for panels
PPE and access equipment as listed in {{business:safety.required_ppe}}, and the Victorian working-at-height method for each roof

commonErrors.error: Pricing from an older per-panel figure
commonErrors.prevention: Build the price from the owner's own hours and access, and use per-panel figures only as a record of past jobs.

commonErrors.error: Counting paid hours as productive hours
commonErrors.prevention: Use chargeable hours only when calculating the cost per productive hour.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out access set-up, photographs and the warranty check
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every estimate.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no exclusions for electrical work or chemicals
commonErrors.prevention: List the electrical work and any chemical not approved for panels as exclusions.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited. State and territory fair trading rules also apply.

Electrical work is outside a cleaning price. Solar Victoria says a system should be serviced by a licensed electrician. The licence scope for cleaning crews was not researched, so check it before any work near electrical equipment.

Victoria: the working-at-height rule for roof access was not checked in this draft. WorkSafe Victoria says allowing workers onto a roof without adequate protection is unlawful, even with no incident. Check the Victorian rule before allowing time for any roof access.
Award, enterprise agreement and on-cost rates for employees are unconfirmed in this research. Check which instrument applies to each worker.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows panel count, storey and access, hours or price basis, the warranty check, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten solar jobs and compared with the estimate.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing array details, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours by task
summary: Panel cleaning is mostly time on the roof and access, so start every quote from hours.
Cost per productive hour uses chargeable time, not paid time.
Access, photographs, the warranty note and any exclusions are named lines.
Do not turn one job's price into a per-panel rate for other sites.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for solar panel cleaning?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker and nothing else from the accounts or the rent
The price the client pays, plus the deposit, the late fee and the crew bonus paid
The average hourly rate of competitors in the local area and their fees for the whole year
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, water and equipment, access equipment, consumables, insurance and administration, divided by chargeable hours

knowledgeChecks.question: A 20-panel job is estimated at 2.5 crew-hours and takes 4. What is the right response?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, since the client has already paid and the crew has finished
Reduce paid hours for the crew on the next job and skip the morning break
Raise the price for this client's next job only and no one else is charged more

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a solar quote need an exclusions list?
options: To hide the margin from the client and to keep the rates a secret from the crew
To make the quote longer and to fill up the page with more text and words for the client
To show what the price covers, such as electrical work and chemicals, so scope changes can be priced and disputes are reduced
To lower the client's expectations and to make the job seem much smaller than it is

sourceReferences: Solar Victoria, 'Maintenance guide', https://www.solar.vic.gov.au/maintenance-guide, updated 17 July 2026. Supports: a licensed electrician services the system; cleaning by the installer or a specialist; water is usually enough.

SolarQuotes, 'Solar panel cleaning', https://www.solarquotes.com.au/blog/solar-panel-cleaning/, published 27 September 2016, last modified 4 June 2025. Only per-panel figure found; 2016 origin; not used as a rate.

WorkSafe Victoria, news release on falls risks in the solar sector, https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/news/2026-08/crackdown-falls-risks-solar-sector, 26 August 2026. Supports: unlawful to allow workers onto a roof without adequate protection, even with no incident.

business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as leave and superannuation belong in the hourly cost.
ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading price statements are prohibited.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours; add a set allowance for delays; figure stated by source of 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work.

Work Health and Safety (Managing the Risk of Falls at Workplaces) Code of Practice 2015, https://legislation.gov.au/F2016L00425/asmade/2016-03-30/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html, registered 2016. Commonwealth code; not Victorian law. Cited for the height point; the Victorian rule was not checked.

Note: award, enterprise agreement and on-cost rules are UNCONFIRMED for solar work. No current per-panel price or solar cleaning hours benchmark was found. The electrical licence scope for cleaning was not researched.
